function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here’s a quick guide to help you find the perfect place to order a cake from—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a convenient online option:

| Option | What it offers | How to find it | Tips |
|--------|----------------|----------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for supporting small businesses | Google “cake shop near me” or check Yelp / Google Maps | Look for bakeries with good reviews & photos; call ahead for availability & delivery hours |
| **National chain bakeries** (e.g., Baskin‑Robbins, Mrs. Fields, Magnolia Bakery) | Consistent quality, sometimes nationwide delivery | Visit their website or use their app | Check if they offer same‑day delivery or pickup; compare prices |
| **Online food delivery platforms** (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates, SkipTheDishes) | Wide selection from many local restaurants & bakeries | Search “cakes” or “desserts” in your city | Filter by rating, delivery time, and price; some platforms let you see real‑time order status |
| **Specialty cake makers** (e.g., artisanal vegan, gluten‑free, custom wedding cakes) | Unique flavors, dietary accommodations, custom designs | Search “custom cake maker” + your city; Instagram & Facebook pages are useful | Ask for a portfolio or sample photos; confirm customization options & lead time |
| **Grocery store delivery** (Instacart, Amazon Fresh, Shipt) | Cakes from in‑store bakeries or pre‑ordered items | Add your address to the service’s app; search for “cakes” | Delivery windows may be longer than restaurant apps; check if they deliver to your ZIP code |
| **Online marketplaces** (Etsy, Shopify stores) | Handmade, often unique designs | Search “handmade cake” + your region | Verify shipping policies & return/exchange terms; read seller ratings |
| **Subscription boxes** (e.g., Goldbelly, Cake Delivery Box) | Curated selections from renowned bakeries across the country | Browse their catalog online | Great for gifts or trying new flavors; usually require advance ordering |

### Quick Steps to Order:
1. **Decide on the type of cake** – birthday, wedding, dietary restrictions, size, flavor, design.
2. **Choose a platform** – local bakery for freshness, or a delivery app for convenience.
3. **Check delivery coverage** – make sure the service delivers to your ZIP code and within your preferred time window.
4. **Place the order early** – especially for custom or large cakes, order at least 24–48 hrs in advance.
5. **Confirm details** – double‑check flavor, size, delivery address, contact info, and any special instructions (e.g., no sugar, vegan frosting).

If you tell me your city or ZIP code, I can look up specific bakeries or delivery options that serve your area. Happy cake hunting!
